h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר נ״א Pesach — Maamar Nun Aleph
The Robe Engraved with Az: You Have Robed Hashem and He Has Robed You

p: בְּיַלְקוּט שִׁמְעוֹנִי
In Yalkut Shimoni
(רמ"א):

אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁאָמְרוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל "אָז יָשִׁיר", לָבַשׁ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא חָלוּק שֶׁל תִּפְאֶרֶת שֶׁהָיָה חָקוּק עָלָיו כָּל "אָז" שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה: אָז תִּשְׂמַח בְּתוּלָה בְּמָחוֹל, אָז יְדַלֵּג כָּאַיָּל פִּסֵּחַ וְכוּלֵּי, אֶת ה' הֶאֱמַרְתָּ הַיּוֹם וַה' הֶאֱמִירְךָ.

"Rabbi Akiva said: At the moment Israel recited 'Then (Az) [Moshe] sang,' the Holy One, blessed is He, donned a robe of splendor upon which was engraved every 'Then' (Az) in Scripture: 'Then shall the maiden rejoice in dance,' 'Then shall the lame leap like a hart,' etc., 'You have affirmed (he'emarta) Hashem today, and Hashem has affirmed (he'emircha) you.'"
אַחַר שֶׁזָּכַר כַּמָּה פְּסוּקֵי "אָז", זָכַר פָּסוּק: אֶת ה' הֶאֱמַרְתָּ, שֶׁלֹּא נִזְכַּר בּוֹ "אָז"!
Now after citing several verses containing the word Az, the Midrash cites the verse "You have affirmed Hashem," in which the word Az does not appear at all!
רַק נִרְאֶה שֶׁמְּפָרֵשׁ "הֶאֱמַרְתָּ" לְשׁוֹן אִימְרָא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּפָרֵשׁ אַחַר כָּךְ: בִּצַּע אֶמְרָתוֹ
Rather, it appears that it interprets he'emarta in the sense of imra (the hem/border of a garment), just as it interprets afterward "He tore His garment (imraso)"
(אֵיכָה ב', י"ז),
(Eichah 2:17),
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה
and as they said in Midrash Rabbah
(אֵיכָה רַבָּה ב', כ"א):
(Eichah Rabbah 2:21):
בָּזַע פּוֹרְפִירִין שֶׁלּוֹ.
"He rent His royal purple robe."
וּמְפָרֵשׁ "אֶת ה' הֶאֱמַרְתָּ" שֶׁהִלְבִּישׁוּ כִּבְיָכוֹל אֶת ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ, דְּמֶלֶךְ בַּעֲשָׂרָה לְבוּשִׁים, וּכְתִיב
Thus it interprets "You have robed (he'emarta) Hashem" as meaning that Israel, as it were, clothed Hashem, may He be blessed—for the King arrays Himself in ten garments, as it is written
(תְּהִלִּים צ"ג, א'):
(Tehillim 93:1):
ה' מָלָךְ גֵּאוּת לָבֵשׁ
"Hashem reigns, He has clothed Himself in majesty"
לְבוּשׁ תִּפְאֶרֶת, דְּאֵין מֶלֶךְ בְּלֹא עָם, וְעַל יְדֵי שֶׁמְּקַבְּלִין מַלְכוּתוֹ נִכְתָּר כִּבְיָכוֹל ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ: כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן דְּאִיהוּ כֶּתֶר מַלְכוּת, וְזֶה נִקְרָא לְבוּשׁ;

a garment of splendor, for there is no king without a people, and through Israel accepting His kingship, Hashem, may He be blessed, is crowned, as it were—for Kesser Elyon is Kesser Malchus—and this is called a garment;
וּלְבוּשׁ הָרִאשׁוֹן: עֹטֶה אוֹר כַּשַּׂלְמָה, וְזֶהוּ: אֶת ה' הֶאֱמַרְתָּ.
and the very first garment is "He wraps Himself in light like a robe," which is "You have robed Hashem."
וְ"ה' הֶאֱמִירְךָ" הַיְינוּ גַּם כֵּן מַה שֶּׁהִלְבִּישָׁם ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ, רוּחַ מִקּוֹדֶשׁ עִילָּאָה; וְרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ נִקְרָא לְבוּשׁ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּדְרָשׁ:

And "and Hashem has robed (he'emircha) you" likewise refers to Hashem, may He be blessed, clothing Israel in Ruach HaKodesh, a spirit from Supernal Holiness—and Ruach HaKodesh is called a garment, as it is expounded:
וַתִּלְבַּשׁ אֶסְתֵּר מַלְכוּת
"'And Esther donned royalty (Malchus)'"
(אֶסְתֵּר ה', א')
(Esther 5:1)
שֶׁלְּבָשַׁתָּה רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ
that Ruach HaKodesh clothed her
(מְגִילָּה י"ד:),
(Megillah 14b),
וְכֵן: וּמָרְדֳּכַי יָצָא בִּלְבוּשׁ מַלְכוּת
and likewise "And Mordechai went out in royal apparel"
(אֶסְתֵּר ח', ט"ו),
(Esther 8:15),
כִּדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
as stated in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ג' קס"ט:).
וּבַגְּמָרָא נִדְרָשׁ
And in the Gemara it is expounded
(בְּרָכוֹת ו'.):
(Berachos 6a):
אֶת ה' הֶאֱמַרְתָּ וַה' הֶאֱמִירְךָ — אַתֶּם עֲשִׂיתוּנִי חֲטִיבָה אַחַת בָּעוֹלָם, וַאֲנִי אֶעֱשֶׂה אֶתְכֶם חֲטִיבָה אַחַת בָּעוֹלָם
"'You have affirmed Hashem and Hashem has affirmed you'—[God says:] 'You have made Me a single unique entity in the world, and I will make you a single unique entity in the world'"

וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁעַל יְדֵי שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל מְקַבְּלִים מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ מַלְבִּישִׁים כִּבְיָכוֹל אֶת ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּלְבוּשׁ מַלְכוּת, אוֹר כַּשַּׂלְמָה, וַ"ה' הֶאֱמִירְךָ" — תְּפִילִּין דְּמָארֵי עָלְמָא דְּמִשְׁתַּבַּח בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכִין יִשְׂרָאֵל לִלְבוּשׁ מַלְכוּת, רוּחַ מִקּוֹדֶשׁ עִילָּאָה.

meaning that when Israel accept His kingship, may He be blessed, they clothe Hashem, as it were, in a royal garment of "light like a robe," and "Hashem has robed you" refers to the Tefillin of the Master of the Universe in which He glories in Israel, whereby Israel merit the royal garment of the spirit from Supernal Holiness.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁאָמְרוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל "אָז יָשִׁיר", לָבַשׁ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא חָלוּק שֶׁל תִּפְאֶרֶת שֶׁחָקוּק עָלָיו כָּל "אָז" שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה
And this is what they meant by saying that at the moment Israel sang "Then (Az) [Moshe] sang," the Holy One, blessed is He, donned a robe of splendor engraved with every Az in Scripture
וּכְמוֹ דְּאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
and as stated in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' נ"ד.)
דְּ"אָז" מוֹרֶה דְּאִתְחַבַּר א' לְז', דְּהַיְינוּ נְהִירוּ דְּעַתִּיקָא לְמִדַּת מַלְכוּת, כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
that Az indicates the union of Alef with Zayin, namely the illumination of Atika uniting with the attribute of Malchus, Knesses Yisrael.
וּמַסִּיק בַּיַּלְקוּט: וְכֵיוָן שֶׁחָטְאוּ חָזַר וּקְרָעוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: בִּצַּע אֶמְרָתוֹ
And the Yalkut concludes: "And once they sinned, He went back and tore it, as it is said, 'He rent His garment (imraso)'"
וְהוּא כְּדְרַשׁ הַמִּדְרָשׁ רַבָּה הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל: בָּזַע פּוֹרְפִירִין דִּילֵיהּ
which follows the Midrash Rabbah's exposition cited above, "He rent His royal purple robe"
וְעָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהַחֲזִירוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
"and in the future the Holy One, blessed is He, will restore it, as it is said
(תְּהִלִּים קכ"ו, ב'):
(Tehillim 126:2):
אָז יִמָּלֵא שְׂחוֹק פִּינוּ.
'Then (az) our mouth will be filled with laughter.'"

וְצָרִיךְ לְהָבִין לָמָּה זָכַר דַּוְקָא פָּסוּק זֶה: אָז יִמָּלֵא, דְּקָאֵי עַל הֶעָתִיד? הֲלוֹא כַּמָּה פְּסוּקִים חָשַׁב מִקּוֹדֶם: אָז תִּשְׂמַח וְגוֹמֵר, אָז יְדַלֵּג וְגוֹמֵר, דְּקָאֵי עַל הֶעָתִיד!

Now one must understand why it cited specifically this verse, "Then our mouth will be filled," regarding the future—surely it had already listed several other verses earlier ("Then shall the maiden rejoice, etc.," "Then shall the lame leap, etc.") that also refer to the future!

אַךְ עִנְיָן שֶׁאָמַר שֶׁעָתִיד לְהַחֲזִירוֹ: אִם הָיָה הַפֵּירוּשׁ "בִּצַּע אֶמְרָתוֹ" שֶׁבָּזַע פּוֹרְפִירִין שֶׁלּוֹ בְּפוֹעַל, אֵין שַׁיָּיךְ "עָתִיד לְהַחֲזִירוֹ", רַק לְשׁוֹן עָתִיד לְתַקְּנוֹ וּלְחַבְּרוֹ!

However, consider the phrase "in the future He will restore it": if "He rent His garment" meant that He literally tore His royal robe apart, the expression "restore it" would not apply—it should have said "mend it" or "stitch it back together"!
אַךְ הוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: בְּשׁוּב ה' אֶת שִׁיבַת צִיּוֹן הָיִינוּ כְּחֹלְמִים—כְּמוֹ חֲלוֹם;
Rather, it follows what is stated just before that verse: "When Hashem brings back the captivity of Zion, we will be like dreamers"—like a dream;
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת לֹא בָּזַע פּוֹרְפִירוֹ וְלֹא נִקְרַע, רַק שֶׁנִּדְמָה כְּקָרוּעַ, אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת הַלְּבוּשׁ שָׁלֵם, וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ שֶׁעָתִיד לְהַחֲזִירוֹ

meaning that in absolute truth He never rent His royal robe and it was never torn—it merely appeared as if torn during exile, whereas in reality the garment remained whole, which is why it says He will "restore/reveal it again"

וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ מִפָּסוּק: אָז יִמָּלֵא שְׂחוֹק פִּינוּ, שֶׁיִּתְבָּרֵר שֶׁלְּבוּשׁ תִּפְאֶרֶת שֶׁחָקוּק עָלָיו "אָז", שֶׁהוּא חִיבּוּר א' לְז', שֶׁהוּא כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, הָיָה שָׁלֵם מֵעִיקָּרוֹ וְלֹא נִקְרַע.

and this is why it brings proof from "Then our mouth will be filled with laughter," because it will become clear that the robe of splendor engraved with Az—the union of Alef with Zayin, Knesses Yisrael—was always intact from the very beginning and was never truly torn.

וְאָמַר אַחַר כָּךְ: אָז יֹאמְרוּ בַגּוֹיִם וְגוֹמֵר—הַיְינוּ הָאוּמּוֹת שֶׁיִּשָּׁאֲרוּ יַכִּירוּ גַּם הֵם שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל הָיוּ תָּמִיד קְשׁוּרִים בַּה' יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "אָז", שֶׁהוּא גַּם כֵּן חִיבּוּר א' לְז'.

And immediately afterward it says, "Then they will say among the nations, etc."—meaning even the surviving nations will recognize that Israel were always bound to Hashem, may He be blessed, which is why it says Az, again signifying the union of Alef with Zayin.
וְכֵן מוֹרֶה: הַזֹּרְעִים בְּדִמְעָה בְּרִנָּה יִקְצֹרוּ וְגוֹמֵר, שֶׁיִּתְבָּרֵר שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה כְּלָל מַה לִּבְכּוֹת
And similarly the continuation "Those who sow in tears shall reap in joy, etc." teaches that it will become clear there was never any reason to weep at all
וּכְעִנְיַן שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא
along the lines of what they said in the Gemara
(תַּעֲנִית ה'.):
(Taanis 5a):
הָלוֹךְ יֵלֵךְ וּבָכֹה וְגוֹמֵר בֹּא יָבֹא בְרִנָּה: שׁוֹר כְּשֶׁהוּא חוֹרֵשׁ הוֹלֵךְ וּבוֹכֶה, וּבַחֲזִירָתוֹ אוֹכֵל חָזִיז מִן הַתֶּלֶם

"'Though he goes along weeping, etc., he shall surely come back with joy': when an ox plows [in the days of Yoel] it goes along weeping, yet on its return trip it already eats green shoots from the furrow"

וְעַל אוֹתוֹ דּוֹר נֶאֱמַר: הַזֹּרְעִים וְגוֹמֵר, שֶׁהָיָה בְּדַעְתָּם שֶׁחַס וְשָׁלוֹם אָבְדָה תִּקְוָה כֵּיוָן שֶׁיָּצָא אֲדָר וְלֹא יָרְדוּ גְּשָׁמִים, וְאַחַר כָּךְ רָאוּ שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה כְּלָל דְּאָגָה, וּתְבוּאָה הַגְּדֵילָה בְּשִׁשָּׁה חֳדָשִׁים גָּדְלָה בְּאַחַד עָשָׂר יוֹם, וְהַדְּאָגָה וְהַבְּכִי הָיָה רַק כַּחֲלוֹם, כַּאֲשֶׁר יַחֲלוֹם אִישׁ וְכוּלֵּי.

and concerning that generation it was said "Those who sow in tears, etc.," for they thought all hope was lost, God forbid, once Adar passed without rain, yet afterward they saw there had been no cause for worry at all, as grain that normally takes six months to grow sprouted in eleven days, so all their anxiety and weeping had been nothing more than a dream.
וְכֵן: בְּשׁוּב ה' אֶת שִׁיבַת צִיּוֹן יִרְאוּ שֶׁלֹּא נִקְרַע הַלְּבוּשׁ מֵעוֹלָם כְּלָל, שֶׁאַף בַּגָּלוּת הָיָה ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ הַמַּנְהִיג וְהַמֶּלֶךְ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר

And so too "When Hashem brings back the captivity of Zion," they will see that the royal garment was never torn at all, for even in exile Hashem, may He be blessed, was the Sovereign and King, as it is said
(יִרְמְיָה מ"ט, ל"ח):
(Yirmiyahu 49:38):
וְשַׂמְתִּי כִסְאִי בְּעֵילָם,
"And I will set My throne in Elam,"
וְכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁגָּלוּ שְׁכִינָה עִמָּהֶם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּמְגִילָּה
and wherever Israel were exiled the Divine Presence went with them, as they said in Megillah
וְהָיָה חִיבּוּר אָלֶ"ף לְזַיִ"ן—וְזֶה שֶׁמֵּבִיא פָּסוּק זֶה: אָז יִמָּלֵא שְׂחוֹק פִּינוּ.
so the union of Alef with Zayin always remained intact—and this is why the Midrash cites specifically the verse "Then our mouth will be filled with laughter."

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Tiferes Yosef, Ki Savo — “‘You have affirmed (he’emarta) Hashem today to be your God, and Hashem has affirmed you today to be His treasured people.’ My grandfather explained that he’emarta is the language of the hem (imrah) of a garment. Just as a garment, as long as it has no hem, is not yet finished and when the hem is finished that is the completion and purpose of the garment, so ‘You have affirmed Hashem today’: since Israel had refined themselves after forty years so that their whole purpose was the honor of Heaven. And therefore ‘Hashem has affirmed you,’ that Hashem shows that His whole purpose is for Israel.” Connection: The same reading of he’emarta as the hem of a garment; the Izhbitzer takes the hem as the completion that fixes the garment, Israel’s finished purpose, where Pri Tzaddik reads it as the royal robe Israel give Hashem.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Maharal, Gevuros Hashem 65 — “When they praised Hashem with ‘Az yashir,’ this praise was that Hashem, blessed be He, is exalted over the world and separate from nature, for the word ‘az’ shows the One riding upon the seven days of creation, which are nature. Therefore with this praise they clothed Hashem in a robe of splendor, for glory too is called a garment, and on this robe was written every ‘az’ in the Torah, all of which show His glory, that He is separate from material nature. This garment comes to Him from the lower beings. When the Temple was destroyed below, there was no longer glory and splendor among the lower beings, and so the robe of splendor He had had from the creatures was torn: ‘He rent His garment.’” Connection: Maharal reads the same Midrash as a garment that Israel’s praise gives to Hashem from below, built on the alef above the seven; Rav Tzadok adds that the tearing was only apparent and the garment was never truly rent.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Ki Savo 10 — “This itself will be a sign and a wonder: that all the kinds of rebuke are only for an hour, on the surface, but in truth the holiness of Israel will remain forever. And this may be hinted in the verse ‘When Hashem brings back the captivity of Zion, we were like dreamers’: that in the future it will be seen plainly that all the rebukes were like a dream, said only to frighten a person so that he would mend his way.” Connection: The same reading of ‘we were like dreamers’, that the exile only appeared to break Israel’s bond, applied there to the curses of the rebuke which are said only to stir repentance.

paragraphs.text: Taanis 5a — of the generation of Yoel, when Adar passed without rain: "Of that generation it says, 'Those who sow in tears shall reap in joy; he goes along weeping, carrying the bag of seed…' Rabbi Yehudah said: When the ox plows, it goes along weeping, and on its return it eats the green shoots from the furrow — and this is 'he shall come back with joy.'" Rashi: for as soon as it is sown it begins to grow.
